name: Meenakshi Raman
scenario_title: The Offer to Join the Evening Gathering
action: Meenakshi pauses, lets the well water drip from her hands, and dries them on the edge of her sari. She glances toward the temple hall, then back at Kamakshi, and speaks softly: "If I can sit among the women and answer what they ask—not stand and speak—I will come. But now I must prepare lunch before the heat. Remind me again on Thursday."
reason: Kamakshi's invitation warmed Meenakshi but also stirred her shyness: the last time she stood at the temple hall was at her youngest son's wedding, where she sat in a corner and said little, and her mother had taught that healing knowledge passes woman to woman in quiet voices, not before a crowd. She also remembered teaching herself to read alone in the kitchen at night because she did not want an audience. Still, she felt the healers' names needed to be told, and she could answer if the women asked her directly, one at a time; she could not stand and speak as though she knew more than them. With lunch still to be made before the afternoon heat, she accepted only on the condition that she could sit among the women and answer their questions rather than address them, and she asked Kamakshi to remind her on Thursday.
